title: Priority-Prober: tier-aware circuit breaker with escalating fallback probes
creator: Manisha Rao
description: Implement a tier-aware circuit breaker that triggers automated fallbacks when upstream signals (429 rate-limits, request timeouts, and elevated error rates) exceed adaptive thresholds. The breaker should be priority-aware (distinguishing paid/dedicated traffic vs best-effort hosted) and include an escalating prober sequence that probes candidate fallback variants (regional replicas, lower-cost quantized models, cached prefix variants) to validate capacity before switching traffic. Goal: reduce user-facing errors and tail latency during overloads while avoiding unnecessary failovers that reduce output quality or increase cost.
acceptance_criteria: Circuit breaker trips when combined signal score (429s, p50/p95 timeout amplification, 5xx error-rate) crosses configurable threshold per-tenant and per-tier
Escalating prober sequence runs automatically within configured cooldown windows and must validate at least one fallback variant with healthy latency/error profile before cutover
Fallback decision includes confidence score and reason code (e.g., RATE_LIMIT_PEAK, REGIONAL_LATENCY_SPIKE, MODEL_OOM)
Telemetry emitted for each state transition (closed -> probing -> open -> soft-recovery) with tenant, tier, region, current model variant, and thresholds used
Chaos + load test scenario: under simulated 429 surge, zero customer-visible 5xx for dedicated-tier traffic and <2% degraded-quality alerts for hosted-tier during 95th percentile events
Rollback capability: manual forced-close and traffic holdback routes available in Console for on-call teams
design_notes: Use additive signal scoring: score = w_429 * normalized_429_rate + w_timeout * normalized_timeout_rate + w_5xx * normalized_5xx_rate; weights default to (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) but configurable per project/tier
Priority-awareness: dedicated/reserved capacity routes should have elevated thresholds and longer hysteresis; hosted/free-tier should be more aggressive to protect latency SLOs of paying customers

Prober escalation: Stage 1 = lightweight health probe to regional replica (single token prefix); Stage 2 = short inference to quantized variant with production prompt set; Stage 3 = cached-prefix candidate check. Each stage records latency, token error heuristics, and sample-quality signal metrics

Safety: require two consecutive successful probes at Stage N (within probe window) before performing full traffic cutover; fallback cutover uses gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on regression
Compatibility: leverage existing smart routing policy API surface so policies can be expressed as JSON configs in routing rules (region selectors, tier weights, fallbacks list)
Persistence: store per-tenant breaker state in consistent kv with TTL-based decay for probation; include decay factor to avoid flapping
Edge cases: treat downstream OOMs and model-specific errors as stronger signals than generic 5xx; differentiate infrastructure-level timeouts (network) vs model generation timeouts
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind runtime-opt-in; deploy master->staging with synthetic workload and integrate with existing telemetry dashboards
2) Canary to 5% of internal paid accounts for 48h with active on-call monitoring and alerting
3) Expand to 25% with a heatmap dashboard showing probe outcomes by region and model variant
4) Enable default behavior for new compute clusters and offer opt-in for existing tenants over two weeks
5) Post rollout: 2-week monitoring with automated quality regression gates; revert flag if >3% increase in quality alerts for paid tenants
comments: 2026-02-13 - Manisha Rao: Kicked off spike to validate probe timings against quantized variants. Found that 2-stage probe median adds ~35ms for Region A; acceptable for staged cutover.

2026-02-20 - Luca Fernandez: Spike results: prefix-cache probes are high-fidelity but sometimes stale for streaming endpoints. Recommendation: require sample-quality check during Stage 2 for streaming models.
2026-02-27 - Manisha Rao: PM review (Eleanor Kim) requested that dedicated-tier thresholds are overridable per-contract; added to design notes and config schema.

2026-03-03 - QA: Ran chaos test with artificial 429 spike. Breaker probed and cutover to quantized fallback with no 5xx for canary tenants, but observed increased hallucination score on one prompt family; created follow-up ENG-820322 for prompt-set adjustments.
2026-03-08 - Security: Reviewed data collection for probe payloads; approved with requirement to redact PII and enforce sample size limits. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-10 - Luca Fernandez: Implementation ready for review. Integration tests green. Requesting review from runtime and console teams for traffic control UI hooks.
